Title: Research Paper
Text:
THE MODULE OF VALABREGA-VALLA OF THE JACOBIAN
IDEAL OF POINTS IN PROJECTIVE PLANE
ABBAS NASROLLAH NEJAD
ZAHRA SHAHIDI
Abstract. The module of Valabrega-Valla of the Jacobian ideal of a reduced pro-
jective variety V is the torsion of the Aluﬃalgebra. One considers the problem
of its vanishing in the case of where V is a reduced set of points in the projective
plane. It is shown that the module is nonzero for several cases of a special con-
ﬁguration class therein – called (s −r)-fold collinear conﬁguration. A complete
classiﬁcation of types is given for 5 and 6 points in regard to this problem.
Introduction
Let V ⊂Pd = Pd
k denote a reduced projective variety over a perfect ﬁeld k,
with homogeneous coordinate ring A = R/J, where R = k[x0, . . . , xd] and J is the
homogeneous deﬁning ideal of V in its embedding. By deﬁnition, the Jacobian ideal
of the k-algebra A is the Fitting ideal of order d + 1 −(d −dim V ) = dim V + 1 of
the module of K¨ahler k-diﬀerentials ΩA/k of A. Since ΩA/k depends only on A, and
not on any particular presentation of A, and so do the Fitting ideals of ΩA/k, then
this notion is dependent only upon the given projective embedding of V . This is as
much invariance one can dispose of.
Now, since ΩA/k admits a module presentation as the cokernel of the transposed
Jacobian matrix Θ of a set of generators of J, modulo J, then the Jacobian ideal
of A is the ideal of A generated by the (d −dim V )-minors of this Jacobian matrix.
By abuse, one often takes the ideal of (d −dim V )-minors back in the polynomial
ring R as the Jacobian ideal of the ideal J. If this malpractice is followed then, in
order to keep the invariant properties of the Jacobian ideal of A, one should always
take those minors summed to J – that is, the ideal I := (J, Id−dim V (Θ)) ⊂R.
In this paper we focus on the problem as to when the so-called Valabrega–Valla
module vanishes for the pair J ⊂I, where J is a homogeneous ideal in a polynomial
ring over a ﬁeld and I, denotes its Jacobian ideal. For that a basic principle was
established in [8, Example 2.19] and successfully applied to a collection of classical
geometric situations, such as the rational normal curve (codimension d −1) and
certain Segre and Veronese embeddings. A little later, this problem was applied
in [10] for special classes of linear determinantal ideals (rational normal scrolls and
alike).

In [9] the problem was circumscribed to the case of a set of reduced points when
the latter admits a minimal set of generators in degree 2.
In [7, Theorem 1.2]
a characterization of the vanishing of the module of Valabrega-Valla was given in
terms of the ﬁrst syzygy module of the form ideal J∗in the associated graded
ring of I. In [13] a vast extension of these matters was taken all the way to the
environment of modules, bringing up some hard features of Cohen–Macaulay and
Gorenstein algebras naturally arising from Rees algebras of modules.

As such, it has appeared elsewhere in a diﬀerent context (see [14], also [15, 5.1]). As
it turns out, provided I has a regular element module J, the Valabrega–Valla module
is the A-torsion of the so-called embedded Aluﬃalgebra of I/J, hence its interest
for the geometric purpose [6]. Dealing directly with the Valabrega–Valla module
makes the structure of the Aluﬃalgebra itself sort of invisible. On the bright side,
in the case where a = I/J is the Jacobian ideal of A = R/J, the heavy work is
transferred to understanding its nature. Besides, for some mysterious reason, the
existence of non-trivial torsion is often delivered at the level of degree 2 of VVJ⊂I.
The Jacobian ideal I/J ⊂A := R/J will be said to be VV-torsion free if VVJ⊂I =
{0}, i.e., if J ∩It = JIt−1 for all t ≥2.
The main goal of this work is to understand the nature of the VV-torsion freeness
of the Jacobian ideal I of an ideal J ⊂R := k[x0, . . . , xn] of a ﬁnite set of distinct
points in projective space. Note that, since R/J is Cohen–Macaulay, R/J is reduced
if and only if ht (I) ≥ht (J) + 1, which is equivalent to saying that J is an ideal
of reduced points if and only if I contains a regular element modulo J or, still, to
assert that I is an m-primary ideal, where m = (x0, . . . , xn). As such, the only
algebraic subtlety away from the geometric data is the number and the degrees of
a set of minimal generators of the m-primary ideal I. Indeed, this emphasis will
prevail throughout the paper.
The results and examples in [9] show that the answer to this problem may not
have a general shape, even when one assumes that the deﬁning ideal is generated
by quadrics – a condition that is only guaranteed when the number of points in Pn
is at most 2n. In P2 this forces the number of points to be at most 4, not a very
bright situation. The idea of this work is to go beyond, by rather focusing on special
conﬁguration of points in the projective plane P2, without imposing constraints on
the number of points. However, we do consider the ‘next’ cases: 5 and 6 points are
completely classiﬁed.
The reason to look at reduced plane points is that, along with the results of [8]
on hypersurfaces, it would give a reasonable picture of the Jacobian torsion for the
subvarietis of P2. The next diﬃcult step would be the case of curves in P3, a problem
that we may tackle in the near future. It is the authors expectation that new suitable
techniques be brought in to get a bird view of the problem in all cases.
The outline of the paper is as follows.

3
In section 1, we give a quick view of the main characters for arbitrary ideals in
a Noetherian ring (for further details we refer to [8]). Then proceed to the case
of the deﬁning ideal of a reduced set of points in projective space. In this regard,
Proposition 1.3 gives a criterion to check VV-torsion freeness of the Jacobian ideal of
a ﬁnite set of points in a projective space.
In section 2, we consider the following conﬁguration of points in P2: given integers
s ≥4 and 0 ≤r ≤s −3, will say that a ﬁnite set of points X is an (s −r)-fold
collinear conﬁguration when (s −r) among them lie on a straight line. We prove
that if r = 0, 1, then the Jacobian ideal of the deﬁning ideal I(X) of X is not VV-
torsion free (Theorem 2.2). In the case that r = 2, s ≥8 or r = 3, s ≥9, we
show that the Jacobian ideal of X is not VV-torsion free. Clearly, all theses cases
have a simple geometry, which however does not seem to yield automatically the
‘asymptotic’ behavior of the problem in consideration.
In section 3 we consider the deﬁning ideal I(X) of a set X of 5 and 6 points in
P2. In the case of 5 distinct points it is known that there are 5 mutually distinct
conﬁgurations. We show that the Jacobian ideal of I(X) is VV-torsion-free exactly
in the following conﬁgurations:
• X is in general linear position.
• X is a 3-fold collinear conﬁguration.
• X is a 3-fold collinear conﬁguration such that the straight line through the
remaining two points intersect in a point of X.
Finally, let X ⊂P2 be a set of six points. For 6 points, there are eleven distinct
conﬁgurations (see Figure 1). We show that the Jacobian ideal of I(X) is VV-torsion-
free if and only if X is in one of the following conﬁgurations:
• X is in general linear position.
• X is a 4-fold collinear conﬁguration.
• X is a 4-fold collinear conﬁguration such that the straight line through the
remaining two points intersect in a point of X.
• X is a 3-fold collinear conﬁguration such that the remaining three points are
in general linear position.
• X is a 3-fold collinear conﬁguration such that the straight line through two
of the remaining points intersect in a point of X.
• X is a 3-fold collinear conﬁguration such that two straight lines through of
the remaining points intersect in points of X.
• X is a 3-fold collinear conﬁguration such that the three straight lines through
of the remaining points intersect in points of X.

The Aluﬃalgebra is an algebraic version of characteristic cycles in intersection
theory [6]. The connection of module of Valabrega-Valla with the Aluﬃalgebra is
as follows:
Proposition 1.1. ([8, Proposition 2.5]) If I has a regular element module J, then
the module of Valabrega–Valla is the R/J-torsion of the Aluﬃalgebra of I/J.
The vanishing of VVJ⊂I has close relation with the theory of I-standard base ( in
the sense of Hironaka), Artin Rees number and relation type number (See [11] and
[10]).
Let X := {p1, . . . , ps} be a set of s distinct points in Pn := Pn

X is the ideal I(X) = Ts

ideal generated by n linear forms. Note that the coordinate ring R/I(X) of X is a
reduced ring of dimension one and hence is a Cohen-Macaulay ring. The multiplicity
of R/I(X) is the number of points in X [2, Corollary 3.10]. Since R/I(X) is locally
regular on the punctured spectrum, by the Jacobian criterion it translates into the
property that the Jacobian ideal I = (I(X), In(Θ)) is m-primary, where In(Θ) is
the ideal of n-minors of the Jacobian matrix Θ of I(X) and m denotes the maximal
irrelevant ideal of the polynomial ring R. In other words, there is a suitable power
ml that lands into I. Therefore, if the deﬁning ideal of X is minimally generated in
single degree m ≥2 and mn(m−1) ⊂I, then the Valabrega-Valla module vanishes [9].
Let us introduce the following terminology:
Deﬁnition 1.2. The Jacobian ideal I/J ⊂A := R/J will be said to be VV-torsion
free if VVJ⊂I = {0}, i.e., if J ∩It = JIt−1 for all t ≥2.
Given a ring A and an ideal a = (a1, . . . , an) ⊆A, one lets ϕ : A[T1, . . . , Tn] ↠
RA(a) = A[at] be the graded map sending Ti to ait. The relation type number of a
is the largest degree of any minimal system of homogeneous generators of the kernel
ϕ. Since the isomorphism A[T1, . . . , Tn]/Kerϕ ≃RA(a) is graded, an application of
the Schanuel lemma to the graded pieces shows that the notion is independent of
the set of generators of a.

A key result in the case of points reads like this:
Proposition 1.3. Let X be a ﬁnite set of s points in Pn and I stands for the Jacobian
ideal of I(X). Assume that I(X) ∩It = I(X)It−1 for every 2 ≤t ≤s. Then the
Jacobian ideal of I(X) is VV-torsion-free.
Proof. By [8, Corollary 2.17] it suﬃces to prove that the relation type number of
I/I(X) is at most s. But as R/I(X) is a 1-dimensional Cohen Macaulay graded ring,
then [12, Lemma 6.3] implies that the relation type number of I/I(X) is bounded
by the multiplicity of R/I(X) which is the number of points in X.
□
Remark 1. (a) By Proposition 1.3, to check the VV-torsion-freeness it is enough to
check for t ≤s, where s is the number of points. This bound is not sharp in general
– see, e.g., Proposition 3.1.
(b) Let X be a set of s collinear points with s ≥4 in P2. Then the deﬁning ideal
of X is I(X) = (z, f(x, y)), where f(x, y) is a reduced product of s linear forms in
x, y. Then the relation type of I/I(X) on R/I(X) is the degree of the dual form
of f(x, y), which is itself (for the details see Proposition 2.2). Thus, the relation
type is s (maximal possible), but I(X) ∩I2 ̸= I(X)I as can be readily obtained by
considering the element y2s−4f.
2. (s −r)-fold collinear configurations in P2
We introduce the following conﬁguration of points in P2.
Deﬁnition 2.1. Let s ≥4 and 0 ≤r ≤s −3 be integers. An (s −r)-fold collinear
conﬁguration is a ﬁnite set of s ≥4 plane points such that exactly (s −r) of its
points lie on a straight line.
Theorem 2.2. Let X ⊂P2 be an (s −r)-fold collinear conﬁguration. If r = 0, 1,
then the Jacobian ideal of I(X) is not VV-torsion free.

{z = 0}. Then the ideal of a point pi(1 ≤i ≤s) has the form I(pi) := (z, ℓi(x, y)), for
some k-linear form ℓi(x, y) ∈k[x, y]. Moreover, these linear forms are independent.

Proposition 1.1, this relation gives a non-trivial torsion.

Abstract: The module of Valabrega-Valla of the Jacobian ideal of a reduced pro- jective variety V is the torsion of the Aluﬃalgebra. One considers the problem of its vanishing in the case of where V is a reduced set of points in the projective plane. It is shown that the module is nonzero for several cases of a special con- ﬁguration class therein – called (s −r)-fold collinear conﬁguration. A complete classiﬁcation of types is given for 5 and 6 points in regard to this problem.
